title: Small Dog Beds

seo_description: Pressed into the sofa cushion or the gap behind your knees? Small dog beds with walls, soft linings and sizes from 45 × 29.5cm. Find one that fits them.

intro_html: The folds of your coat, the gap behind your knees, the corner of the sofa cushion. These small dog beds give them an edge of their own, sized so they're tucked in, not lost.
description_html:
Watch a small dog settle. They turn, turn again, then press themselves into the smallest space on offer. A small dog bed works when it gives them that edge to tuck against and something soft to burrow into, without being so big that they end up adrift in the middle of it.

Small dog beds by how they settle

  • If they burrow and curl, choose walls and a soft middle. Sawrey has a sherpa-pile lining and starts at an XS of 45 × 35cm. Harewood is velvet with a cushioned rim, from 46 × 36cm. Thirlmere has structured felt walls that stay upright when they lean into them. More walled shapes are among our nest and donut dog beds.
  • If they rest a chin, choose a rim at the right height. Blea Tarn is cream bouclé with a raised rim, from 60 × 50cm.
  • If they need firmer support, often as they get older, choose foam. Chatsworth has a crumb memory foam base and bolster walls. Kendal puts a memory foam core under corduroy, from 45 × 29.5cm.

Sizing a small dog bed

Go by the sleeping area, not the outside. On a nest or bolster bed the walls take up a real share of the footprint: Chatsworth's Small is 55 × 40cm outside but 38 × 27cm inside. Measure your dog curled up as well as stretched out, and if they're between sizes, size up.

One thing to know: this collection includes every bed that comes in a Small or XS, and some of those beds also come much bigger. Ullswater's Small, for example, is 63 × 77cm. Check the centimetres on the size you pick. The size guide has the full method.

What makes a small bed feel right

Walls give them something to press against. A lining such as sherpa, velvet or fleece gives a soft surface the moment they step in. A non-slip base, as on Chatsworth and Loweswater, stops a light bed sliding across a smooth floor when they jump in.

100 nights to settle in

Some small dogs are particular about where they sleep, so there is time to let them decide. Most beds here come with the 100-night sleep trial: within 100 nights, if it isn't right, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. Two exceptions: the Rydal Personalised bed is made to order with your dog's name, so it is excluded from the trial and from change-of-mind returns, and the Whinlatter car seat is a travel accessory, so check its returns terms before ordering. Free standard UK delivery on orders over £40.

Small dog bed questions

Which size for a pug, dachshund or Yorkie?

Some beds name breeds against each size. Elterwater's Small lists pugs, French bulldogs and dachshunds; Kentmere's Small lists Yorkshire terriers, chihuahuas and Pomeranians. Use that as a starting point, then measure your own dog.

Does a small dog need an orthopaedic bed?

Not automatically. Many beds here are soft fibre-filled nests by design. If yours is getting stiffer, foam such as Chatsworth or Kendal gives firmer support, and our beds for older dogs are worth a look. If they seem to be in pain, talk to your vet; a bed is comfort, not treatment.

Can I machine wash a small dog bed?

The covers on Sawrey, Harewood, Blea Tarn and Loweswater unzip and wash at 30°C. Thirlmere's felt structure shouldn't go in the machine. Always follow the sewn-in label.

Want a shortcut? Answer a few quick questions in the Bed Finder, sleep style first, and you get one bed to look at.
